subject: Hosted API POC: access scope, endpoints & rate plan
messages:
From: Samir Khan <samir@finlytics.ai>
To: irene_choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Olivia Turner <olivia.turner@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2026-12-20T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Thanks + hosted POC ask and a couple clarifying items

Hi Irene —

Thanks for the demo this morning. Olivia and I chatted and we want to move forward with a short hosted POC to validate throughput/latency for our ingestion pipeline and spot-check costs. A few quick questions so we scope correctly: 

- Can you confirm what an initial sandbox endpoint looks like (hosted API only) — separate URL per model?
- What rate limits/soft quotas do you typically apply for POCs and is bursting allowed?
- What's the preferred way to test tokenized usage and get a rough cost estimate for 100M tokens/month?
- We need to understand data residency — EU vs US options — our primary users are in US.

We can fill any access form needed; target start next week if possible.

Thanks,
Samir
Head of ML Engineering
FinLytics Labs
[Attachment: poc_requirements.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

From: irene_choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Khan <samir@finlytics.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-20T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Thanks + hosted POC ask and a couple clarifying items

Samir — great to hear you want to proceed. Quick recap and proposed next steps below.

Recap of asks: hosted-only POC, validate endpoints/latency for ingestion, confirm ratecap and cost for ~100M tokens/mo, US residency.

Proposed next steps (timeline to start next week):
1) We provision a sandbox hosted endpoint (single URL) mapped to a recommended model variant. Sandbox will allow up to 50 concurrent connections with a baseline soft rate of 60 requests/sec and token-level throttles.
2) Marissa will send our POC access form and the exact endpoint matrix (including hostname, auth method). Please return the signed form and a short traffic profile (avg tokens per request, peak TPS).
3) We’ll provide a provisional cost estimate for 100M tokens based on your traffic profile and suggested batching/caching knobs.
4) Vivek will outline expected latency ranges and recommended concurrency/kv-cache settings to stay within SLOs.

Attachments: poc_access_form.pdf (it contains required fields for billing & network allowlisting) and sandbox-endpoint-matrix.csv.

If this looks good I’ll ask Marissa to open the sandbox and set an initial ratecap that we can adjust after 48h of telemetry.

—Irene
Irene Choi
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0132

On 2026-12-20 09:12, Samir Khan wrote: > Thanks for the demo this morning...

From: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Khan <samir@finlytics.ai>, irene_choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: vivek_kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-20T13:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API POC: access scope, endpoints & rate plan — access form + endpoint details

Samir — adding operational detail so you can hand to your infra/security teams quickly.

What we will provision for the POC (hosted API):
- Single sandbox URL: https://sandbox-api.redwood.ai/finlytics-poc (API key auth).
- Models: gpt-redwood-2-small (default) and gpt-redwood-2-medium (optional). We can swap later.
- Rate profile (initial): 60 reqs/sec aggregate, 50 concurrent long-polling streaming responses. Token throttles at 180k tokens/min. Burst policy: +30% for 10s windows, subject to telemetry and fair-use.
- Logging & telemetry: request-level latency and token counts visible in the Console; we retain telemetry for 14 days on trial.

Please complete the attached poc_access_form.pdf with billing contact, allowlist IPs, and preferred start window. Also attached sandbox-endpoint-matrix.csv for your records.

If you expect higher TPS during ramp (>200 reqs/sec) let us know and we’ll provision a dedicated burst lane for the trial (might require a short separate commit).

Marissa Cole
Product Ops, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: poc_access_form.pdf (fillable PDF)]

From: vivek_kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, irene_choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Samir Khan <samir@finlytics.ai>
Date: 2026-12-20T16:01:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API POC: latency expectations and concurrency guidance

Quick notes from an infra/reliability perspective so FinLytics can size clients correctly: 

- Expected median p99 latency for gpt-redwood-2-small with the sandbox rate profile is ~120-180ms per token generation step for 512-token outputs; end-to-end request latency will depend on prompt length and total tokens.
- For deterministic latency, use our streaming response with smaller chunk sizes and enable KV-prefix caching if you send repeated context.
- If you need to simulate sustained 100M tokens/month during the POC, plan for batching on the client to hit cost targets. We can provide a client-side batcher example.
- For security: hosted US-region only for this POC; we can evaluate EU regional tenancy if needed for production.

Irene/Marissa — flagging that if FinLytics signs the access form and expects >150 reqs/sec we should discuss a temporary dedicated burst lane.

—Vivek
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

From: Samir Khan <samir@finlytics.ai>
To: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, irene_choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-21T14:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API POC: access scope, endpoints & rate plan — confirmed next steps

Thanks — this is perfect context. We completed the poc_access_form.pdf (attached) and included our expected traffic profile: avg 800 tokens/request, peak 220 reqs/sec for short windows, typical sustained 45 reqs/sec. We also provided allowlist IPs.

Next for us: finalize NDA with legal this week (sending separately), then we want the sandbox provisioned Tue morning PST. We accept the hosted US-region for the POC. Please open the sandbox and set the initial ratecap Marissa suggested; we'll monitor and escalate if we need burst capacity.

Olivia (cc'd) will coordinate the billing & network questions.

Best,
Samir
[Attachment: completed_poc_access_form.pdf (signed PDF)]
